subject: Re: Pilot options — application-layer anonymization + short log window
messages:
From: Peter Wong <peter.wong@mediquest.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Lena Chen <lena.chen@clinicnova.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — data handling constraints

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and the blockers we need to resolve before a pilot:

- Hard requirement: no long-term storage of raw patient-identifiable transcripts. We need either 0-retention for raw inputs or guaranteed application-layer redaction that removes/replaces PII before any logs are persisted.
- Short-term diagnostic logs are acceptable only if anonymized and TTL <= 14 days.
- Data residency: EU routing for EU patients; still evaluating whether we need an on-prem option for a subset of flows.
- Compliance evidence: can you provide SOC 2 scope pages and an example audit report excerpt that shows logging/retention controls?

Lena and I want to see a concrete proposal (technical approach + timeline + tradeoffs). Can Redwood support a short pilot that demonstrates anonymization in production traffic without retaining PII?

Next steps: please send proposed configurations and any pilot artifacts. Also include who from your side we should loop into procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Peter
Senior Product Manager
MediQuest Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Peter Wong <peter.wong@mediquest.io>
Cc: Dr. Lena Chen <lena.chen@clinicnova.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — data handling constraints

Hi Peter (and Lena),

Appreciate the clear summary — helped our team prioritize the pilot constraints. High-level proposal attached (redwood-privacy-offer.pdf) and a short pilot scope doc (privacy-pilot-scope.docx). Summary below:

Proposal (concise):
- Application-layer anonymization at ingestion: customer-side SDK (or proxy) performs deterministic token redaction + stable hashed IDs before sending to Redwood. This ensures PII never reaches persistent logs in cleartext.
- Short log window: store service-level logs (request/response metadata + hashed IDs) for 14 days. No long-term transcript retention. KV cache for model acceleration kept for up to 72 hours by default; we can set to 0 for the pilot if desired.
- 0-retention variant: for the strictest flows we can enable ephemeral mode — no transcript or model input is written to any persistent store; only in-memory serving with N-minute ephemeral caches. Tradeoffs: higher cold-start latency and reduced ability to debug edge cases.
- Data residency: route EU patient traffic to our eu-west region (we have GDPR controls in place). For an on-prem requirement we can scope a Private deployment, but that is a separate procurement path.

Compliance evidence: attached soc2-summary.pdf (high level) and we can provide an SOC 2 excerpt under an NDA if procurement/legal need it.

Proposed pilot plan (2–4 weeks):
1) Week 0: alignment call + access/keys + test traffic shape.
2) Week 1: implement ingestion redaction SDK (we'll pair with your engineers).
3) Week 2: run masked traffic to our staging pilot; collect metric/latency reports and masked logs for your review.
4) Week 3: optional short production pilot with monitoring and rollback policy.

Tradeoffs & observations:
- Application-layer redaction is the strongest guarantee we can deliver quickly. It requires changes to your client/service to remove PII before transit.
- If you can't change the client, Redwood can provide a proxy that performs redaction, but it adds a maintenance surface and extra cost.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Aditya (CC'd) will scope the SDK/proxy work and provide an implementation ETA.
- Marcus (CC'd) is the solution lead and will coordinate the pilot runbook.
- I'll send a one-pager for procurement with pricing for a 30-day pilot + optional Private deployment quote.

Action items for MediQuest:
- Confirm interest in application-layer redaction pilot (yes/no).
- Share a point of contact for procurement/legal.
- Indicate whether EU residency is required for the pilot traffic.

Attaching the two docs now. Happy to jump on a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
From: Dr. Lena Chen <lena.chen@clinicnova.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Peter Wong <peter.wong@mediquest.io>
Date: 2025-11-04T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — data handling constraints

Thanks, Stephanie — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifications:

- When you say "deterministic token redaction + stable hashed IDs" — will the hash be reversible by MediQuest for linked session debug? Or is it one-way? Our need: correlate events across services without exposing PII to Redwood engineers.
- For EU routing: can you confirm whether the processing and any short-term logs will remain inside eu-west? We need that isolation for pilot participants in the EU.

If the hash is one-way and you can guarantee EU-only processing for EU traffic, we should be able to proceed with the pilot. Please let us know if an on-prem short-term pilot would materially change timelines/pricing.

Lena
Clinical Data Lead
ClinicNova (partnering with MediQuest)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Lena Chen <lena.chen@clinicnova.com>, Peter Wong <peter.wong@mediquest.io>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T10:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — data handling constraints

Hi Lena, Peter — quick technical clarifications from the infra side:

- Hashing: we recommend using a deterministic, salted one-way hash that you manage (salt held by MediQuest). That way you can correlate across your services without Redwood being able to reverse the hash. If you prefer Redwood-managed stable IDs, we can provide pseudonymous IDs but we'd treat those as internal identifiers and they wouldn't be reversible.
- EU residency: when traffic is tagged for eu-west tenancy, both inference and short-term metadata logs (the 14-day window) are stored in EU-only tenants and encrypted with region-scoped KMS. We can provide the region tenancy diagram on the tech deep dive.
- Ephemeral mode: enabling 0-retention for transcripts routes everything through in-memory-only paths; this avoids writing to persistent logs and KV caches can be disabled. Note: disabling KV caching increases token costs and end-to-end latency for repeated prompts because we can't reuse cached KV state.

I'll upload a short diagram and the TTL knobs to the shared Drive link (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3Cprivacy-pilot). Marcus will handle the pilot runbook and I'll provide a rough ETA for the SDK/proxy (3–5 business days for an initial PoC).

Aditya
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

- We are okay to proceed with the application-layer redaction pilot. We'll own the salt for the one-way hash and provide a POC service to exercise redaction.
- Lena will coordinate a short legal check; procurement contact is me (I'll loop in legal & InfoSec if they request the SOC excerpt).
- Please send over the pilot runbook and proposed calendar. The week-after-next tech deep dive sounds good.

I'll schedule a 30-minute slot for the deep dive and invite your team. Thanks,
Peter
